🐛 Treat the keep mask as a predicate in masked sum

Masked sum multiplied each element by its mask value, while size(),
front() and apply() treat any nonzero mask value as "keep". As a result
array({1, 2, 3}).keep(array({2, 0, 3})).sum() returned 11 instead of 4,
and an excluded infinity or NaN made the sum NaN, as 0 * inf is NaN.

Select with mask != 0 ? value : 0, which also covers the boolean branch.
The result type is now decltype(1 * value), as in the domain::zero
shortcut just above, so it no longer depends on the mask's type: int
values with a double mask now sum to int instead of double.
